Abase
uh-BASE
verb
From Old French abaisser, to lower; in Scripture, to bring low the proud or to be brought low in estate, often under God’s hand.

📖 Biblical Definition

To abase is to bring low. Scripture uses the word for God’s humbling of the proud and for the believer’s being made low in outward estate. Job is challenged to cast abroad the rage of wrath and abase every one that is proud. Ezekiel hears the LORD’s sentence: exalt him that is low, and abase him that is high. Paul testifies that he knows both how to be abased and how to abound, having learned contentment in Christ in every state. Our Lord adds that whosoever shall exalt himself shall be abased, and he that shall humble himself shall be exalted. The doctrine is unified. Pride is the posture God resists; lowliness is the school in which grace often teaches. Abase is not self-hatred. It is the refusal of self-exaltation, and the patient endurance of providential reduction without charging God foolishly. Kings lose crowns, the rich learn hunger, and the apostle learns the secret of sufficiency in the One who strengthens him. The church that will not be abased will not be trusted with true exaltation, for God giveth grace unto the humble and will in due time lift them up.

📜 Webster 1828 Definition

To bring low; in Scripture, God’s humbling of pride and the saint’s being lowered in estate under providence.

expand to see more

ABASE, to cast down, humble, or bring low.

God abases the proud and exalts the low.

Paul knew how to be abased and how to abound.

The word opposes self-exaltation and restless status.

True abasing is under God’s hand, not theatrical self-contempt.

📖 Key Scripture

Job 40:11 — "Cast abroad the rage of thy wrath: and behold every one that is proud, and abase him."

Eze 21:26 — "Thus saith the Lord GOD; Remove the diadem, and take off the crown: this shall not be the same: exalt him that is low, and abase him that is high."

Php 4:12 — "I know both how to be abased, and I know how to abound: every where and in all things I am instructed both to be full and to be hungry, both to abound and to suffer need."

Mat 23:12 — "And whosoever shall exalt himself shall be abased; and he that shall humble himself shall be exalted."

⚠️ Modern Corruption

Modern culture either abases no one (pride as virtue) or abases everyone (shame as identity); Scripture abases pride and comforts the lowly in Christ.

expand to see more

The first corruption is the gospel of self-esteem that treats every lowering as abuse. Paul’s being abased is not trauma identity; it is discipleship in contentment. The second corruption is cruel humiliation culture that delights to tear down without righteousness. God abases the proud for truth’s sake, not for sport. A third soft form is performative self-abasement that seeks praise for humility. Scripture cuts all three: fear God, refuse pride, and learn Christ in high and low estate.

Therapy speech makes abasement a pathology; status speech makes pride a right. The biblical word answers both. To be abased under God can be mercy. To refuse all abasing is rebellion. The saint prays to be kept low enough to obey and high enough in Christ to hope.

🔗 Greek & Hebrew Roots

Abase means to bring low: God’s judgment on pride and the believer’s training in low estate.

expand to see more

English — abase, to lower or humble.

Latin root stream — related to lowering / bringing down.

Providence — estates rise and fall under God.

Moral — pride invited abasement; humility invites grace.

Christ — contentment in Him in abasement and abundance.

Usage

"God will abase the proud and exalt the low."

"Paul learned how to be abased and how to abound."

"The saint accepts providential lowering without pride or despair."
